title: Azure Resource Lock Changes

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `mscs:azure:audit` events with `resourceId="*providers/Microsoft.Authorization/locks*"` into `index=azure`. Confirm UC-4.2.44 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `mscs:azure:audit` traffic without `resourceId="*providers/Microsoft.Authorization/locks*"`. Confirm UC-4.2.44 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=azure` sourcetype=`mscs:azure:audit` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:audit" resourceId="*providers/Microsoft.Authorization/locks*"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.44_azure_resource_lock_chan_44"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.2.44 — Azure Resource Lock Changes: queries Microsoft Azure `mscs:azure:audit` for search criteria `resourceId="*providers/Microsoft.Authorization/locks*"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On Microsoft Azure, detecting 'Azure Resource Lock Changes' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.2.44 drives high-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Alert on Delete or write operations against lock resources. Require change ticket in comments where possible. Correlate with subsequent delete operations on parent resources.
visualization: Table (operation, user, resource group), Timeline (lock changes).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Change.All_Changes
  by All_Changes.user All_Changes.object_category All_Changes.action span=1h

dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Change (All_Changes).
knownFalsePositives: Our own break-glass and automation accounts show up the same as anyone else, and a delete or write during a change window is expected. We allowlist the roles that do routine maintenance and we link alerts to approved changes before we call an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` with the modular input for `mscs:azure:audit`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Alert on Delete or write operations against lock resources. Require change ticket in comments where possible. Correlate with subsequent delete operations on parent resources.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:audit" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:audit" resourceId="*providers/Microsoft.Authorization/locks*"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.44_azure_resource_lock_chan_44"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `mscs:azure:audit` in `index=azure` to detect azure resource lock changes. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_44_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (operation, user, resource group), Timeline (lock changes)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of azure resource lock changes so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
